definitions.meaning: A feeding level in a food chain or web: producers are the first level, herbivores the second, and carnivores the levels above.
A sequence of trophic levels showing who eats whom, with arrows pointing in the direction of energy flow, from food to feeder.
All the interlinked food chains in a community, showing every feeding pathway energy can take.
A diagram of the energy at each trophic level, narrowing upwards because only about 10% of energy moves up each level.
An organism, usually a green plant, that captures sunlight by photosynthesis and feeds the whole food chain or web.
An organism that obtains energy by eating other organisms: primary consumers eat producers, secondary consumers eat herbivores.
An organism that breaks down dead matter and waste, releasing carbon and other matter back into cycles.
The cycling of carbon between air, living organisms and decomposers: photosynthesis draws CO2 in, respiration and combustion return it.

mechanismSteps: Food chains: arrows follow energy flow: a chain runs producer to primary consumer to secondary consumer, and arrows point from food to feeder, the way energy moves.
Food webs: one dot splits into two: one producer can feed several consumers and one consumer can have several foods, so energy splits across interlinked pathways.
Pyramid of energy: only 10% moves up: most energy is lost as heat and waste, so each level keeps only a tenth and food chains stay short.
The carbon cycle: one dot, round and round: photosynthesis draws CO2 into plants, respiration and combustion return it to the air, and decomposers release carbon from dead matter.
Conservation: when habitat shrinks, species vanish: fragmentation isolates small populations, and protected corridors reconnect fragments so species can move again.
A common mistake: energy is not recycled: energy flows one way and leaves as heat, while matter such as carbon is what actually cycles.
objectives: Describe energy flow through food chains, food webs and pyramids of energy
Explain the carbon cycle, conservation and why energy is not recycled
subject: science
title: JC H2 biology — ecology: energy flow and the carbon cycle

trap.explanation: The "cycle of life" language makes energy sound like it loops round forever. Energy flows one way - sunlight in, heat out: what is recycled is matter - carbon, nitrogen and water. In the animation scene s6 the red energy dot enters as sunlight and leaves as heat, never returning, while the blue carbon dot loops round and round: matter cycles, energy does not.
trap.misconception: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem.

workedExample: In scenes s1 and s3, the chain grass -> rabbit -> fox follows the energy arrows, and if producers hold 10 000 kJ, only about 1 000 kJ reaches the rabbits and about 100 kJ reaches the foxes. Each step multiplies by a tenth - the 10% rule - so the pyramid narrows and there is too little energy left to support longer chains.
